Get one transition network per latent group class, to compare how their members move between profiles

Source: R/tna.R
get_group_tna.Rd

get_group_tna() returns one transition network per latent group class, as a grouped object of the tna package, so that the group classes can be compared on how their members stay in and move between profiles. Every network has the same nodes, the profiles (classes) profile_1, profile_2, and so on, and its edge weights are the probabilities of moving from one profile to another at the next occasion.

Where the probabilities come from depends on the model:

  • for a transition fit from lta(), each network is the transition matrix the model estimated for that group class, and starts from the class's estimated initial probabilities;

  • for a profile or class fit made with time, the groups are split by their assigned (most likely) group class, and tna::group_tna() counts each network from the sequences of assigned profiles of the groups in that class.

Usage

get_group_tna(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multilpa_transitions'
get_group_tna(x, label = "Group class", ...)

Arguments

x

A transition fit from lta(), or a profile or class fit made with time. See Which fits are supported.

...

Further arguments passed to tna::tna() for each class of a transition fit, or to tna::group_tna() for a profile or class fit.

label

One string: what the classes are called in the names of the networks and in tna's output (default "Group class", which gives "Group class 1", "Group class 2", and so on).

Value

An object of class group_tna: a named list of tna networks, one per latent group class, each as get_tna() describes. The grouped functions of the tna package apply to it: centralities() returns one table with a group column, compare() contrasts two classes, and plot() draws every network.

Conditions raised: latents_no_time, latents_unsupported_tna and latents_not_a_fit as described under Which fits are supported; latents_missing_package when the tna package is not installed; latents_bad_argument when label is not one string; and the warning latents_empty_transition_row.

Details

A transition-matrix row with no expected moves out of its profile keeps its fitted probabilities, and a warning of class latents_empty_transition_row says that the row is not estimated from transitions.

Which fits are supported

The same fits as get_tna(), and mover-stayer fits as well:

  • An lta() fit of class multilpa_transitions: always.

  • An lta() fit of class multilpa_lta: when its transitions are first order, the same at every occasion and without transition covariates; otherwise it raises latents_unsupported_tna.

  • A mover-stayer fit (mover_stayer = TRUE): one network per mover class and one named "Stayers", whose matrix is the identity.

  • A profile or class fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca() (with or without membership covariates): when it was made with time; without it the fit raises latents_no_time.

  • Any other model raises latents_not_a_fit.

Interpretation

The networks describe latent group classes, not the individual observed groups. Networks counted from assigned profiles treat both the profile and the group-class assignments as known and carry the uncertainty of neither.

See also

get_tna() for one network over the whole sample; plot_transitions() for the transition matrices as a plot.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("tna", quietly = TRUE)) {
  activity <- c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read")
  moves <- lta(course_engagement, vars = activity, id = "student",
               time = "sequence", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2,
               n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
  get_group_tna(moves)
}
